s: The Mazdayasnian religion is described as good and having a long descent.

l: holy creatures of the Spenta Mainyu, Yasna, Yasna IV.
s: The holy creatures of the Spenta Mainyu, male and female, are included among those to whom offerings are announced and presented.
Asha is identified as the lofty lord who is the ritual righteousness itself. Asha receives offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.

l: Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, Yasna, Yasna IV.
s: The holy Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma receives offerings and is identified as a saint.
Zarathustra Spitâma is associated with a holy Fravashi who receives offerings.
The good Yazads, earthly and heavenly, receive offerings because of Asha Vahista and are described as fit for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.
Yasna V. consists only of a note stating that this chapter is identical with Yasna XXXVII. It concerns the relationship between Yasna V. and Yasna XXXVII. No other content or details are provided.
Yasna V. is identified as a chapter that is identical with Yasna XXXVII.
Yasna XXXVII is identified as identical with Yasna V.

Yasna VI continues the sacrifice with fuller expression by worshipping Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the lords of the ritual order, and many divine beings and sacred things. It concerns Mithra, Fire (Ahura Mazda's son), Sraosha, the Fravashis of the saints, Mãthra Spenta, the Mazdayasnian Religion, Haoma, Zarathustra, waters, plants, lands, mountains, festivals, and celestial bodies. The text concludes with the Ratu and the Zaotar speaking about the Ratu from Righteousness.
Yasna VI presents a fuller continuation of the sacrifice, naming the beings, sacred things, places, times, and observances that are worshipped.

The sacrifice worships Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the lords of the ritual order, divine beings, sacred waters and plants, mountains, festivals, the Fravashis of the saints, and other Mazda-made things.

Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the Creator and as radiant, glorious, good, valiant, and bountiful. He is also identified with the lord of the district and is said to have made the Fire, waters, plants, mountains, glory, benefit, and Sanctity.

Mithra is worshipped as being of the wide pastures, with a thousand ears and myriad eyes, and as the Yazad of the spoken name. He is also worshipped with Ahura as one of the lofty, imperishable, and holy two, and is called the province-lord of all the provinces.
Fire is worshipped as Ahura Mazda's son and as a holy lord of the ritual order. It is worshipped together with all the fires, wood-billets, perfume, and the good, Mazda-made, holy waters.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna VI.
s: The Fravashis of the saints are described as good, heroic, and bountiful. They are worshipped in the sacrifice, including together with the stars, moon, sun, and Ahura and Mithra, and the sacred Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma is also worshipped.

Sraosha is described as Obedience, blessed and stately, and as smiting with the blow of victory and making the settlements advance. He is worshipped with the sacrifice as a holy lord of the ritual order.

l: three and thirty lords, Yasna, Yasna VI.
s: The lords of the ritual order are repeatedly worshipped throughout the sacrifice. They include the thirty and three who approach nearest around about at Hâvani, whose observances were inculcated by Ahura Mazda and uttered forth by Zarathustra, as well as many other named beings.
Mãthra Spenta is worshipped as glorious and true. It is identified with the law revealed against the Daêvas, the Zarathustrian law, and its long descent.
The Mazdayasnian Religion is worshipped as good. It is named together with Mãthra Spenta and the Zarathustrian law.
Haoma and the Haoma-juice are worshipped in the sacrifice. Haoma is named alongside the sacred Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, the wood-billets, perfume, and Fire.

Zarathustra is named as the one who uttered forth the observances of the thirty and three lords of the ritual order. The text also identifies the sacred Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma and names the Zarathustrian law.

Yasna VII presents offerings and blessings made by the priest for Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha, the Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, the Fire, the waters which are Mazda-made, and many other holy beings and sacred things. It names ritual offerings including the Myazda meat-offering, Haurvatât, Ameretatât, the Kine of blessed gift, Haoma, Haoma-juice, wood-billets, perfume, and the Baresman. It invokes the holy Yazads, the ritual lords of times and places, the Fravashis of the saints, celestial bodies, the Zarathustrian law, the good Religion, and the Mazdayasnian faith. The unit concludes with prayers for protection and reward, sacrifices to the Ahuna-vairya and other sacred prayers, and a declaration of sacrifice to righteous male and female beings.
Yasna VII presents the priest's complete and sacred offerings, blessings, invocations, and sacrifices to Ahura Mazda, the holy Yazads, sacred beings, and ritual powers.
Ahura Mazda is the chief recipient of offerings and propitiation. He is named as the maker of the waters and plants, the father of the Fire, and the one who appoints rewards and ruling protection.
Haurvatât, who guards the water, is offered with the meat-offering and the flesh of the Kine of blessed gift for propitiation.
Ameretatât, who guards the plants and the wood, is offered with the meat-offering and the flesh of the Kine of blessed gift for propitiation.
The Bountiful Immortals are among those for whose propitiation offerings are made. The Baresman and its Zaothra are also offered for their propitiation.

Sraosha is described as blessed, endowed with sanctity, victorious in striking, and causing the settlements to advance. Offerings are made for his propitiation, including the Myazda meat-offering and the flesh of the Kine of blessed gift.
Zarathustra Spitâma is identified as a saint, and offerings of Haoma and Haoma-juice are made for the propitiation of his Fravashi.
The Fire is addressed as Ahura Mazda's son. Wood-billets with perfume are offered for its propitiation, and offerings are made to it together with all the fires.
The waters which are Mazda-made receive offerings of Haoma, Haoma-water, fresh milk, and the plant Hadhânaêpata. They are also included among the waters and sacred things offered to.
The flesh of the Kine of blessed gift is offered with Haurvatât and Ameretatât for the propitiation of Sraosha. It is also included among the things sacrificed to the Ahuna-vairya and sacred prayers.
Haoma is offered with a complete and sacred offering for the propitiation of the Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma and for the good waters which are Mazda-made.
Haoma-juice is offered for the propitiation of the Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma and is included among the things sacrificed to sacred prayers.
Wood-billets with perfume are offered for the propitiation of the Fire. They are also included among the things sacrificed to the good and pious Prayer for blessings.

l: Prayer for blessings, Yasna, Yasna VII.
s: The Prayer for blessings is described as good and pious and is offered with sanctity. It is included among the sacred things sacrificed to, along with the Ahuna-vairya and other offerings.
The holy Yazads, heavenly and earthly, receive offerings for their propitiation when they are meet for sacrifice and homage because of Asha who is Vahista.
Hâvani is named as a holy lord of the ritual order and as the time at which certain lords of the ritual order are approached. Thirty and three lords approach nearest round about Hâvani.

Mithra is described as having wide pastures, a thousand ears, and myriad eyes, and as the Yazad of the spoken name. He is also named with Ahura as lofty and imperishable and as the lord of the provinces.

l: Righteousness the Best, Yasna, Yasna VII.
s: Asha Vahista is identified as Righteousness the Best and is offered to together with Frâdat-fshu, the Zantuma, and Ahura Mazda's Fire.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna VII.
s: The Fravashis of the saints receive offerings, including offerings made to the ancient lore and next of kin. They are also named with Ahura Mazda as those who name the month.
The stars are described as creatures of Spenta Mainyu and receive offerings. The stars, including those without beginning to their course, are included among the sacred things blessed.
The Moon is named as a holy lord of the ritual order in its new, waning, and full forms. It is also said to contain the seed of cattle in its beams.
The Sun is described as resplendent, fleet-horsed, and the eye of Ahura Mazda, and it receives an offering together with Ahura and Mithra.
Mãthra Spenta is described as holy, effective, revealed against the Daêvas, and is offered to with a complete and sacred offering.
The Zarathustrian law is named with Mãthra Spenta and is included among the sacred objects receiving a complete and sacred offering.
The good Religion is described as having a long descent and is identified with the Mazdayasnian faith.

l: good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna, Yasna VII.
s: The Mazdayasnian faith is named as the faith of the good Religion and receives an offering through the mention of its long descent.

Righteousness is named as Asha Vahista, the Best, and as the basis through which Ahura Mazda knows superior fidelity and sanctity. The speaker seeks ruling protection from Ahura Mazda and Righteousness forever.
The Myazda meat-offering is offered with Haurvatât, Ameretatât, and the flesh of the Kine of blessed gift for the propitiation of Sraosha.

l: Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, Yasna, Yasna VII.
s: The Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma receives the offering of Haoma and Haoma-juice and is identified with the saint Zarathustra Spitâma.
All the good Yazads, heavenly and earthly, are offered to as beings meet for sacrifice and homage because of Asha who is Vahista.

The Ahuna-vairya is among the sacred things sacrificed to, together with the veracious word correctly uttered, the good and pious Prayer for blessings, Haurvatât, Ameretatât, the Kine of blessed gift, Haoma, Haoma-juice, wood-billets, and perfume.

The unit concerns the offering of the Myazda and the faithful partaking of it under the guidance of Righteousness. It presents Righteousness as the Best and calls for offerings to Ahura Mazda, Haoma, the waters, plants, and other sacred beings. The Ratu commands deserving men to eat, while Mazdayasnians are urged to practice and teach the Religion of Ahura. Zarathustra prays for the freedom of the holy and the repression of the wicked, and the Zaotar speaks before the Ratu.
Righteousness is called the Best and is associated with weal. The offering is made in its praise, and its practice is connected with liberality, sovereignty, freedom, and glory.
The Myazda is a meat-offering presented with a complete and sacred offering. The Ratu commands men who have deserved it by their righteousness and correctness to eat it.
Haoma and its juice are offered for the praise of Ahura Mazda and other sacred powers. Haoma is also propitiated for sacrifice, homage, and praise as bringing Righteousness.
Ahura Mazda is praised in connection with the offerings and the sacred words. He is asked to reign at His will with a saving rule over His creatures.
The Ratu commands deserving men to eat the Myazda. The Ratu also speaks of the Zaotar as an Ahû to be revered and chosen.
The Mazdayasnian law is addressed with the Bountiful Immortals, just men and women, and Zaothras. It is connected with teaching those who desire to practice the liberality of Righteousness.
The Zaothras are addressed among the sacred participants in the instruction of Mazdayasnians. They are associated with the waters and plants in causing such people to be further taught.
Mazdayasnians are called to practice the liberality of Righteousness and to adhere to the sacred words. Their adults are warned that failure to do so brings them toward the magician's word.
The waters are among the sacred beings over which the holy man is to have sovereignty at his will. They are also named with the plants and Zaothras as part of the instruction of Mazdayasnians.
The plants are among the sacred beings over which the holy man is to have sovereignty at his will. They are associated with the Zaothras and waters in further teaching Mazdayasnians.

The holy man is to become sovereign at his will over waters, plants, and clean and sacred creatures containing the seed of Righteousness. He is to be absolute in power and is prayed for freedom and glory.
The wicked are to be stripped of all power and bereft of all free choice. They are prayed to suffer repression and shame and to be hemmed in without power over any wish.

Zarathustra declares that he will incite the heads of houses, villages, Zantus, and provinces to follow the Religion of Ahura in thought, word, and deed. He also prays for the holy and against the wicked.

l: good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna, Yasna VIII.
s: The Religion of Ahura is described as the religion that Zarathustra urges leaders of houses, villages, Zantus, and provinces to follow. Its practice is expressed through thoughts, words, and deeds.
The Zaotar is described as speaking forth to the Ratu as an Ahû to be revered and chosen. The Zaotar's speech is repeated in the concluding exchange.

The Hôm Yast recounts H(a)oma’s revelation to Zarathustra and the blessings, powers, and protections associated with him. H(a)oma names Vîvanghvant, Âthwya, Thrita, and Pourushaspa as the first four men who prepared him for the corporeal world, describing the sons born to them, including Yima, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, and Zarathustra. The unit recounts victories over dragons, tyrants, demon-gods, and other enemies, and asks H(a)oma for health, strength, prosperity, wisdom, victory, and protection. It also connects Mazda and the Mazdayasnian Faith with H(a)oma and invokes H(a)oma’s mace against forces that harm the righteous saints and settlements.

l: The Hôm Yast, Yasna, Yasna IX.
s: The Hôm Yast concerns H(a)oma, his preparation for the corporeal world by four men, the blessings he grants, and his power against death, enemies, and destructive beings.

H(a)oma comes to Zarathustra while he serves the sacred Fire and identifies himself as holy and driving death afar. He grants or is asked for inspiration, strength, victory, health, healing, prosperity, wisdom, protection, good offspring, knowledge, husbands for maidens, and success against enemies. He lowers Keresâni from his throne and is invoked to hurl his mace at dragons, tyrants, and other destroyers of righteousness.

Zarathustra encounters H(a)oma, questions him about his worshippers, praises him, and asks him for many blessings and protections. He is identified as the son of Pourushaspa, the first reciter of the Ahuna-vairya, and the one who caused the demon-gods to vanish into the ground.
Vîvanghvant is the first man who prepared H(a)oma for the corporeal world. He received the blessing that Yima would be born to him.

Yima, son of Vîvanghvant, is called brilliant, glorious, and the possessor of many flocks. Under his rule, herds and people were free from dying, plants and waters from drought, and people could eat imperishable food; there was neither cold nor heat, age nor death, nor demon-made envy.
Âthwya is the second man who prepared H(a)oma for the corporeal world. He received the blessing that Thraêtaona would be born to him.
Thraêtaona, born to Âthwya, belongs to the heroic tribe. He smote the three-jawed, triple-headed, six-eyed dragon Dahâka.

l: the dragon Dahâka, Yasna, Yasna IX.
s: The dragon Dahâka is three-jawed, triple-headed, six-eyed, and endowed with a thousand powers and mighty strength. He is a lie-demon of the Daêvas, harmful to settlements and the homes of Asha, and was made by Angra Mainyu as a mighty Drug(k) against the corporeal world.
Angra Mainyu made the dragon Dahâka as the most mighty Drug(k) against the corporeal world and for the murder of settlements and the destruction of the homes of Asha.
Thrita, called the most helpful of the Sâmas, is the third man who prepared H(a)oma for the corporeal world. He received the blessing that Urvâkhshaya and Keresâspa would be born to him.

Keresâspa is the son of Thrita and a youth of great ascendant, ringlet-headed, and bludgeon-bearing. He smote a poisonous green horny dragon that swallowed men and horses, though he fled when the dragon sprang up from the boiling water after he cooked meat on its back.
Pourushaspa is the fourth man who prepared H(a)oma for the corporeal world. He received the blessing that Zarathustra, the just and D(a)êva’s foe, would be born to him.
The Ahuna-vairya was first recited by Zarathustra, who intoned it four times with verses kept apart and with an increasingly louder voice.
The D(a)êvas are among the beings whose angry hate Zarathustra asks H(a)oma to overwhelm. They are also named among the enemies against whom H(a)oma’s protection is sought.
Mazda bore to H(a)oma the star-bespangled, spirit-made, ancient Mazdayasnian Faith girdle.

l: good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna, Yasna IX.
s: The Mazdayasnian Faith is described as an ancient, spirit-made girdle borne by Mazda to H(a)oma. H(a)oma wears it on mountain summits for spreading the precepts and headings of the Mãthra and for helping the Mãthra’s teacher.

l: the corporeal worlds, Yasna, Yasna IX.
s: The corporeal world is the realm for which H(a)oma was prepared by Vîvanghvant, Âthwya, Thrita, and Pourushaspa. The dragon Dahâka was made as a Drug(k) against it.
Death is driven afar by H(a)oma. Under Yima’s rule there was neither death nor age, and H(a)oma is asked to grant long vitality and the best life of the saints.
The righteous saints are associated with the best life and radiant heaven sought from H(a)oma. H(a)oma is asked to hurl his mace at beings whose actions cause a righteous saint to perish.

The settlements are harmed by Dahâka and threatened by enemies, tyrants, and invading hosts. H(a)oma is asked to grant Zarathustra power among them and to protect them from violent and wicked persons.
The demon-gods once flew about the earth in human shape and power. Zarathustra caused them all to vanish into the ground.

The unit concerns H(a)oma, its growth, praise, healing powers, and ritual use. It describes H(a)oma growing on mountains and being carried by birds to high peaks, where it appears in milky-white and golden forms. H(a)oma is said to bring victory, health, friendship, prosperity, and protection from curses and death. Zarathustra praises Mazda-made H(a)oma, its plants, teachings, and ritual words, and also praises Righteousness and the Kine.

H(a)oma grows on mountains and is praised for its healing, victorious, health-bringing, friendship-making, and prosperity-giving powers. It is pressed, mixed with milk, poured between vessels, offered in ritual, and invoked to drive away wasting, death, curses, malice, and harmful beings. Zarathustra praises H(a)oma as Mazda-made, along with its plants, songs, teachings, and truthful ritual words.

Zarathustra speaks praise to Mazda-made H(a)oma and praises all its plants on mountains, in valleys, and in clefts. He pours H(a)oma from a silver cup into a golden chalice and asks not to spill its sacred liquor.
Mountains are described as the places where H(a)oma grows, with branches spreading across their heights. Birds carry H(a)oma to high peaks, gorges, abysses, and snow-covered summits.
Righteousness is associated with H(a)oma, which is called its spring and the source of ritual fountains. A faithful praiser of H(a)oma is said to be better than Righteousness the Best.

The cow, horse, and H(a)oma curse those who misuse or withhold them. An offering of tongue and left eye is said to have been chosen by Ahura for H(a)oma, and those who deny it face misfortune in their household. Zarathustra praises H(a)oma as Mazda-made and offers himself to H(a)oma and the sacred exhilaration it bestows. The speaker affirms the value of good thoughts, good words, good deeds, and Righteousness.
The cow curses the driver who feeds her fairly but uses her for selfish fattening rather than for a wife or children.
The horse curses the rider who does not pray for swiftness in crowded competition and who tries to stretch racers to full speed.

H(a)oma curses the drinker who withholds its full outpouring and says it is not a head-smiter but holy and far from death. H(a)oma receives an offering of tongue and left eye, is praised as effective and Mazda-made, and is asked to grant the best world of the saints. H(a)oma is also said to have bound Frangrasyan fast in iron.
Ahura chooses the tongue and left eye as set-apart portions for H(a)oma's meal. Mazda gives the offering to bless H(a)oma, and H(a)oma is praised as Mazda-made.
Frangrasyan, described as a fell Turanian and murderous robber, is said to have been bound fast in iron by H(a)oma.
Zarathustra speaks after the curses and praises H(a)oma as made by Mazda. The speaker identifies with Zarathustra's order.
The offering consists of the tongue and left eye chosen by Ahura for H(a)oma's meal. Anyone who denies, consumes, or withholds it is threatened with household misfortune.
Good thoughts are praised and presented as offerings, while evil thoughts are repudiated.
Good words are praised and presented as offerings, while evil words are repudiated.
Good deeds are praised and presented as offerings, while evil deeds are repudiated.
Righteousness is praised, and it is called a blessing and the Best.

Yasna XII (Sp. XIII), titled The Mazdayasnian Confession, presents a confession of allegiance to Mazda-worship and Zarathustra's order. It rejects the Daêvas, their shelter, headship, thoughts, words, actions, seed, sorcerers, and adherents. It praises Ahura Mazda, Piety, Asha, the Kine, the waters, plants, and the Mazdayasnian villages, while rejecting robbery, violence, drought, wandering, wasting, and withering. It affirms the religious sanctity, Faith of Mazda, and Zarathustrian creed associated with Zarathustra, Kavi Vîstâspa, Frashaostra, Gâmâspa, and future Saoshyants.

l: Yasna XII (Sp. XIII)., Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: Yasna XII (Sp. XIII) contains The Mazdayasnian Confession, in which the speaker declares allegiance to Mazda-worship and Zarathustra's order. It records rejection of the Daêvas and praise of Ahura Mazda, Piety, Asha, the Kine, the villages, and the Faith of Mazda.

l: The Mazdayasnian Confession, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: The Mazdayasnian Confession declares the speaker to be a Mazda-worshipper of the order of Zarathustra and estranged from the Daêvas. It praises the well-thought thought, the word well spoken, the deed well done, and the Faith of Mazda.

The Daêvas are driven away and abjured as evil, bereft of good, deceitful, wicked, and like the Demon-of-the-Lie. Their shelter, headship, thoughts, words, actions, seed, sorcerers, adherents, and iniquitous associates are all rejected.

Zarathustra is identified as the founder of the order to which the speaker belongs. He is described as having abjured the shelter and headship of the Daêvas in his questions and consultations with Ahura Mazda.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: Ahura Mazda is praised as good, endowed with good possessions, holy, resplendent, and glorious. He is credited with making the Kine and holy men, conversing with Zarathustra, and indicating religious matters to him.

l: Mazdayasnian villages, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: The Mazdayasnian villages are protected from robbery, violence against the Kine, drought, wasting, and withering. The speaker declares that he will never become a source of their wasting or withering.

The Kine belong to Ahura Mazda and are associated with Asha and the blessed religious sanctity. The speaker rejects robbery and violence against them and wishes to remove wandering from them as they abide steadfastly upon the land.
Asha (the righteous order pervading all things pure) is identified as belonging to Ahura Mazda. The speaker bows in worship to it and dedicates offerings with praise.

l: religious sanctity, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: The religious sanctity to which the waters, plants, and Kine of blessed gift appertain is also the sanctity to which the speaker belongs. The speaker likewise belongs to the sanctity of Ahura Mazda, who made both Kine and holy men.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: The Faith of Mazda is praised as a holy, imposing, best, and most beautiful religion, including the faith of kindred marriage. It is described as having no faltering utterance and as wielding the felling halbert.

l: Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas, Yasna, Yasna XII (Sp. XIII).
s: The Zarathustrian creed is identified with Ahura's Faith and the Faith of Mazda. The speaker praises it as the best and most beautiful of religions existing or yet to come to knowledge.

Yasna XIII invokes Ahura Mazda, the Mazdayasnian Faith, divine and human leaders, the earth, and other sacred beings. It offers worship, sacrifice, gifts, prayers, and confessions of debt to Ahura Mazda and the Bountiful Immortals. The unit recalls that the two spirits thought, spoke, and acted, and it associates approach to Ahura Mazda with good kinship, Righteousness, thrift-law, and Piety. It also worships several Fravashis and sacred figures, and concludes with worship of the Ahuna-vairya and Asha Vahista and sacrifice to Hâ fraoreti.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: Ahura Mazda is invoked as the supreme recipient of worship, sacrifice, gifts, prayers, and confessions of debt. He is said to have thought, spoken, disposed, and done all things good, and the Kingdom belongs to him to provide nurture to the poor.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Mazdayasnian Faith is invoked, described as blessed and good, and associated with the chief of women. Its sciences, forces, fire-priests, charioteers, warriors, and tillers are also invoked.

l: Fire of Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Fire of Ahura Mazda is invoked as the lord of the friendly and most helpful person.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are summoned and offered the flesh of the speaker's frame and all the blessings of life. They are described as ruling and disposing aright.

l: the two spirits, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The two spirits are said to have thought, spoken, and acted.

Righteousness is described as good and as a kinship through which the worshippers would approach Ahura Mazda. The Right is called the best blessing, bringing weal to the person who acts rightly toward Best Righteousness.

l: Fravashi of the Kine of blessed gift, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Fravashi of the Kine of blessed gift is worshipped.

l: Gaya Maretan (the life-man), Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The holy Gaya Maretan is worshipped through his holy Fravashi.

l: Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: The holy Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma is worshipped.
Zarathustra Spitâma is identified through the worship of his holy Fravashi, and he is called the saint.
The Ahuna-vairya is worshipped.

l: Righteousness the Best, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: Asha Vahista is worshipped as the best, or possibly best, Bountiful Immortal.

l: Hâ fraoreti, Yasna, Yasna XIII (Sp. XIV).
s: Hâ fraoreti receives sacrifice as the confession and laudation of the Mazdayasnian Faith.

Yasna XIV (Sp. XV) presents dedications to the Bountiful Immortals and the holy beings of the ritual order. The speaker offers praise, priestly service, recitation, sacrifice, homage, bodily flesh, and the blessings of a prospered life. The speaker approaches the holy Yazads and identifies as a Mazdayasnian of Zarathustra's order. The Zaotar and Ratu then speak about the Zaotar and the Ratu's righteous authority to speak forth.

l: Yasna XIV (Sp. XV), Yasna, Yasna XIV (Sp. XV).
s: Yasna XIV (Sp. XV) contains dedications, offerings, ritual identifications, and dialogue between the Zaotar and the Ratu.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna XIV (Sp. XV).
s: The Bountiful Immortals receive the speaker's praise, priestly service, invocation, sacrifice, homage, dedication, and sanctification. The speaker dedicates the flesh of the body and the blessings of a prospered life to them.
The Zaothra is used with the Baresman as the speaker approaches the holy Yazads with praise.
The Baresman is used together with the Zaothra in the speaker's approach to the holy Yazads.

l: holy Yazads, Yasna, Yasna XIV (Sp. XV).
s: The speaker approaches the holy Yazads with praise in the Zaothra ritual with the Baresman.

l: holy lords of the ritual order, Yasna, Yasna XIV (Sp. XV).
s: The speaker approaches all the holy lords of the ritual order at their appointed times, including Hâvani, Sâvanghi, and Vîsya.
The speaker confesses to being a Mazdayasnian.
The speaker identifies with Zarathustra's order.

l: Zarathustra's order, Yasna, Yasna XIV (Sp. XV).
s: The speaker confesses to belonging to Zarathustra's order.
The Zaotar speaks in the ritual dialogue and is described as speaking forth in relation to an Ahû and the Ratu. The Zaotar is also said to speak forth when the Ratu is righteous, holy, and learned.
The Ratu speaks in the ritual dialogue and is described as an Ahû to be chosen. The Ratu is instructed to speak forth from his Righteousness as holy and learned.

Yasna XV (Sp. XVI), titled The Sacrifice Continues, concerns the worship of the Bountiful Immortals and the continuation of the sacrifice. The speaker calls upon the Bountiful Immortals with precept, praise, delight, and blessings from the good ritual and Mazdayasnian Faith. The speaker worships those who have lived and continue to live by their names, while choosing the Good Kingdom. Sraosha (Obedience) is invited to be present for the sacrifice of Ahura Mazda, and the Âtarevakhsha calls for the Ratu to speak from righteousness.

l: Yasna XV (Sp. XVI), Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: Yasna XV (Sp. XVI) is titled The Sacrifice Continues. It presents calls, praises, worship, and invocations connected with the sacrifice.

l: The Sacrifice Continues, Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: The Sacrifice Continues concerns the ongoing sacrifice, the worship of the Bountiful Immortals, and the presence of Sraosha (Obedience).

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are called upon with precept, praise, delight produced by grace, and blessings. They are also called beautiful by name and are sacrificed to with the blessing of the good ritual.

l: The Sacrifice, Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: The sacrifice is offered to the Bountiful Immortals with the blessing of the good ritual and the earnest blessings of the good Mazdayasnian Faith. Sraosha (Obedience) is invited to be present for the sacrifice of Ahura Mazda.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: The Mazdayasnian Faith is described as good, and its earnest blessings accompany the sacrifice.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XV (Sp. XVI).
s: Ahura Mazda is described as most beneficent and holy. The sacrifice is offered to Ahura Mazda, for whom Sraosha (Obedience) is asked to be present.
Righteousness provides the best gift associated with the offering, which Ahura knows. The Ratu is called upon to speak from his righteousness.
Sraosha (Obedience) is invited to be present for the sacrifice of Ahura Mazda. He is described as holy, most beneficent, and dear to the speaker at the first and at the last.

This unit concerns the sacrifice and worship of Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, and many heavenly and earthly Yazads. Ahura Mazda is praised as the holy lord of the ritual order, creator of good creatures, and giver of beneficent gifts. Zarathustra Spitâma is worshipped along with his Fravashi, utterances, religion, faith, and lore. The dwelling-place is identified with the bountiful Âramaiti and is asked to provide a healthy home where helpful influences may remain through summer and winter.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XVI (Sp. XVII).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the holy lord of the ritual order, the greatest and most beneficent Yazad, and the creator of good creatures. He is also worshipped as the creator of the Fire, waters, the soul of the Kine, the Wind, and the dwelling-place.
Zarathustra Spitâma is worshipped in the sacrifice as the holy lord of the ritual order. His Fravashi, utterances, religion, faith, and lore are also worshipped.

The dwelling-place is addressed as the bountiful Âramaiti and as the abode of Ahura Mazda. It is described as a home of healthy herds and healthy men, and the worshipper asks that helpful and preserving influences meet him there and remain for summer and winter.

l: The Sacrifice, Yasna, Yasna XVI (Sp. XVII).
s: The sacrifice continues with increased fulness of expression through offered Zaothras and truthfully or faithfully delivered words. It includes worship of Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, the Yazads, the former religions devoted to Righteousness, and other holy beings and creations.

Worship is offered to Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, heavenly and earthly Yazads, the former religions devoted to Righteousness, and various holy creations. It is performed with offered Zaothras and truthfully or faithfully delivered words.

This unit concerns worship of the Fire, waters, plants, sacred words, mountains, prayers, and holy beings. The Fire is honored as Ahura Mazda’s son and through several named fires, including Nairya-sangha. The Mazda-made and holy waters and plants are worshipped, along with Mãthra-spenta and the Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas. Mount Ushi-darena, other holy mountains, prayers, and the Fravashis of the saints are also praised, invoked, and glorified.

The Fire is worshipped as Ahura Mazda’s son and as the holy lord of the ritual order. Several fires are named and worshipped, including Berezi-savangha, Vohu-fryâna, Urvâzista, Vâzista, Spenista, Nairya-sangha, and the fire that is house-lord of all houses.
Ahura Mazda is named as the father of the Fire, which is called his son. The waters, plants, Mount Ushi-darena, and other sacred things are described as Mazda-made.
The good and best waters are worshipped as Mazda-made and holy. All waters that Mazda made and that are holy are included in the worship.

l: plants which Mazda made, Yasna, Yasna XVII.
s: All plants that Mazda made and that are holy are worshipped.
Mãthra-spenta, described as the bounteous word-of-reason, is worshipped.

l: Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas, Yasna, Yasna XVII.
s: The Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas and its long descent are worshipped.
Mount Ushi-darena is worshipped as Mazda-made and shining with holiness.

l: Fravashis of the saints (ancient lore), Yasna, Yasna XVII.
s: The good, heroic, and bountiful Fravashis of the saints are praised, invoked, and glorified. Those of the house, the Vîs, the Zantuma, the Dahvyuma, and the Zarathustrôtema are included.
Nairya-sangha is identified as the Yazad of the royal lineage and is worshipped. All the holy Yazads are praised, invoked, and glorified.

The speaker asks Mazda, who is described as the maker of the Kine, plants, and waters, to grant Immortality. The speaker also asks Mazda to grant Weal and Spirit bounteous. The unit concerns Mazda and the requested gifts of Immortality, Weal, and Spirit bounteous.
Mazda is described as the maker of the Kine, plants, and waters. Mazda is asked to grant Immortality, Weal, and Spirit bounteous.
Immortality is requested from Mazda.
Weal is requested from Mazda.
Spirit bounteous is requested from Mazda.

Yasna XIX. presents Ahura Mazda’s commentary on the Ahuna-vairya, the sacred formula pronounced before creation and containing the seed of righteousness. Zarathustra asks about its origin, power, wording, and meaning, and Ahura Mazda explains its spiritual effects and structure. The text identifies its measures with good thought, good word, and good deed, and connects it with four classes and five chiefs. It concludes with a sacrifice to the parts, memorized recital, chanting, and use of the Ahuna-vairya in the full Yasna.

Yasna XIX. is a commentary on the Ahuna-vairya and explains its origin, wording, measures, classes, chiefs, spiritual power, and proper recitation. It concludes by offering sacrifice to the Ahuna-vairya and its memorized recital, chanting, and use in the full Yasna.

Ahura Mazda tells Zarathustra that the Ahuna-vairya was pronounced before the sky, waters, land, creatures, and the entire corporeal world. He says that reciting it correctly has great spiritual value and can bring a soul across the Bridge of Kinvat to Heaven, while omitting parts draws the soul away from the better world. He is presented as the creator, ruler, and source of the creatures, the Kingdom, and the nourishment of the poor.

Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which word existed before the sky, waters, earth, creatures, and all good creation. He receives an explanation of the Ahuna-vairya and its meaning, structure, and proper performance.

The Ahuna-vairya is the word pronounced by Ahura Mazda before creation and is said to contain the seed of righteousness. Its correctly recited parts are valued above other stanzas, while recitation with omissions or additions has lesser but still stated effects. It has three measures, good thought, good word, and good deed, and is associated with four classes, five chiefs, and a concluding gift.

l: Righteousness the Best, Yasna, Yasna XIX.
s: Righteousness the Best is presented as the principle for which the Ahuna-vairya is learned and recited. The creatures who place Righteousness the Best before all other things perform the deed well done.

The creation is described as existing before, emerging into existence, and yet to be, with its actions devoted to Mazda. Ahura Mazda is said to have pronounced the Ahuna-vairya before the creation of the heaven, waters, plants, four-footed cattle, holy man, and the sun.

Yasna XX. presents commentary on the Ashem Vohû, identifying Righteousness as the best blessing and connecting it with weal. It attributes the prayer’s qualities and words to Asha and Ahura Mazda, and explains how the worshipper ascribes the Mãthra and righteousness to Asha Vahista and the prophets. A catechetical addition describes Mazda’s announcement of a holy one who is heavenly and earthly, and of a holy, best man who rules without capricious tyranny. The passage concludes with sacrifices to the parts, recital, memorising, chanting, and sacrificial use of the Asha Vahista prayer.
Yasna XX. gives a Zand, or commentary, on the Ashem Vohû and includes a catechetical addition concerning Mazda’s announcements and the Asha Vahista prayer.

The Ashem Vohû is described as proclaiming that Righteousness is the best blessing and that there is weal for the man whom the Right helps. Its words are explained through the attribution of blessedness, the Mãthra, and righteousness, and its parts are worshipped, recited, memorised, chanted, and used sacrificially.
Ahura Mazda is said to have spoken forth the words of the Ashem Vohû. Every word and the entire utterance of the prayer are identified as the word of Ahura Mazda.

Righteousness is called the best blessing and is associated with weal. The worshipper ascribes the entire Mãthra and the kingdom to Righteousness, and righteousness is ascribed to the invoking saint and to the prophets.
The prophets are described as recipients to whom righteousness is ascribed, and as those who shall help and bless the people.

l: holy one announced by Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XX.
s: The holy one announced by Mazda is described as both heavenly and earthly.

l: man announced by Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XX.
s: The man announced by Mazda is described as holy and best, and as one who rules without capricious tyranny.

Yasna XXI. is a Catechetical Zand, or commentary upon the Yênhê Hâtãm. It explains that the Yasna and sacrificial worship are offered to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and all holy beings, including male and female saints. It presents questions and answers about salvation, stating that Ahura grants salvation and that Mazda, the best One, answers with the best and holy answer. It identifies the YêNhê hâtãm as a prominent and holy Yast.
Yasna XXI. is presented as a Catechetical Zand concerning the Yênhê Hâtãm. It explains the offering of the Yasna and sacrificial worship and discusses salvation and the best answer given by Mazda.
The Catechetical Zand is a commentary upon the Yênhê Hâtãm. It explains to whom the Yasna is addressed and interprets the questions and answers about salvation.
The Yênhê Hâtãm is described as a piece to which worship is offered. It is called a prominent and holy Yast.
Zarathustra, the saint, is named as the speaker of a word for the Yasna.
Ahura Mazda recognises superior fidelity by reason of sanctity. He is described as the absolute ruler who grants salvation, and the Yasna is offered as his command or institution.

The saints are among those to whom the Yasna and sacrificial worship are offered. The text says that every saint who exists, is coming into existence, or shall exist in the future is answered with the state of salvation.

l: holy females headed by Âramaiti, Yasna, Yasna XXI.
s: The holy females who have Âramaiti at their head are offered sacrificial worship as homage to the Immortals.
The Bountiful Immortals are identified as the recipients of the Yasna in the course of the Yasna.
The Yasna is described as sacrificial worship of Mazda and as an offering made by the worshipper. It is offered to the Bountiful Immortals and to holy beings.
Sacrificial worship is offered to Ahura Mazda, the holy females headed by Âramaiti, the Immortals, and holy beings. The worshipper offers it as if with the beings who are destined to live.
Salvation is the answer given to every saint who exists, is coming into existence, or shall exist in the future. Ahura is asked to grant the state of salvation.

The Sacrifice continues with offerings and praise directed to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and other holy beings and things. The Baresman, Zaothras, Haoma, fresh milk, Hadhânaêpata, Haoma-water, mortars, wood, and perfume are approached with praise and sanctity. The rites seek the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Fire, the beneficent waters, the Mazdayasnian Faith, Mãthra Spenta, and many other sacred powers. The unit also invokes the Gâthas, prayers for blessings, the memorised recital and fulfilment of the Mazdayasnian law, and all good Mazda-made objects.
The Sacrifice continues through ritual approaches, praises, offerings, and acts of propitiation directed toward Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and other sacred beings and objects.
Ahura Mazda is called the Creator, resplendent and glorious. The rites seek his propitiation, as well as that of his Fire and the good things he made.
The Bountiful Immortals are among those for whose worship the Baresman, Zaothra, Haoma, milk, and Hadhânaêpata are approached. Their propitiation is sought in the ritual.

The Baresman is brought together with the Zaothra for worship. Its plant is approached with praise, prayers for blessings, memorised recital, the fulfilment of the Mazdayasnian law, and the heard recital of the Gâthas.
The Zaothras are approached with praise as offerings for the beneficent waters. They have Haoma, milk, and Hadhânaêpata with them and are lifted up with sanctity.
Haoma is approached with praise and sanctity. It accompanies the Zaothras, and its water is also approached with praise for the beneficent waters.
Hadhânaêpata is approached with praise as a plant lifted up with sanctity. It accompanies the Zaothras and the Haoma.

l: good waters which Mazda created, Yasna, Yasna XXII.
s: The beneficent waters are honored through praise offered to the Zaothras and to the Haoma-water.
The Mazdayasnian Faith is associated with its good fulfilment, its heard recital of the Gâthas, and its long descent. Its propitiation is sought in the ritual.
Fire is addressed as Ahura Mazda's son. Its wood and perfume are approached with praise, and its propitiation is sought together with that of all the fires.
Mãthra Spenta is described as bounteous, holy, and effective, instituted against the Daêvas. Its propitiation is sought in the ritual.

This unit concerns the Fravashis of the Saints and prayers for approaching them with praise and worship. It names the Fravashis of houses, villages, communities, provinces, Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Gaya Maretan, Zarathustra Spitâma, Kavi Vîstâspa, Isat-vâstra, and other holy persons. The Fravashis are said to hold heaven, water, land, cattle, and children in the wombs safely apart. The speaker also approaches the Fravashi of his own soul and all good Yazads because of Righteousness the Best.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna XXIII.
s: They are approached with praise and worship. Their Fravashis include those of ancient lore, next-of-kin, pious women, girls, and maidens diligent among the cattle.

l: prayers for the approach of the Fravashis, Yasna, Yasna XXIII.
s: They express the speaker’s desire to approach the Fravashis with praise, worship, Yasnas, and homage.

l: Fravashis of the saints (ancient lore), Yasna, Yasna XXIII.
s: They include the Fravashis of houses, villages, communities, provinces, Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Gaya Maretan, Zarathustra Spitâma, and other holy persons. They hold heaven, water, land, cattle, and children in the wombs safely enclosed apart.
His Fravashi is approached by the speaker with praise and worship.
Their Fravashis are approached by the speaker with praise, together with all the holy Fravashis of the heavenly Yazads.

l: Gaya Maretan (the life-man), Yasna, Yasna XXIII.
s: His Fravashi is approached by the speaker in worship with praise.
His Fravashi is approached by the speaker in worship with praise.
They are approached with praise, including the heavenly and earthly Yazads who are meet for sacrifice and homage.

l: Righteousness the Best, Yasna, Yasna XXIII.
s: The speaker approaches the good Yazads because of Righteousness the Best.

Yasna XXIV. presents Haomas, Zaothras, the Baresman, Hadhânaêpata, food, milk, ritual objects, prayers, recollection, and other Mazda-made objects in worship. These are presented to Ahura Mazda, the good waters, the Fire of Ahura Mazda, Sraosha (Obedience), the Bountiful Immortals, and the Fravashis and souls of the saints. The offerings also concern Zarathustra Spitâma, people who love Righteousness, unborn men, future prophets, and the progress and renovation of the world. The unit associates the offerings with sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and the seed of Righteousness.

Yasna XXIV. describes the presentation of ritual offerings, prayers, recollection, and Mazda-made objects to Ahura Mazda, the good waters, divine beings, the Fravashis and souls of the saints, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.

Ahura Mazda receives presentations of Haomas, Myazdas, Zaothras, the Baresman, flesh, milk, Hadhânaêpata, ritual objects, prayers, and all good Mazda-made objects. He is addressed as the maker of the good objects and as the father of the Fire.
Haoma is presented to Ahura Mazda and to the good waters. Haoma accompanies the Zaothras and is used in Haoma-water.
Zaothras are presented to Ahura Mazda and to the good waters having the Haoma with them. They are included among the offerings made with sanctity.

The Baresman is spread with punctilious or scrupulous sanctity and is presented as an offering. Its plant is also presented along with prayers, recollection, wood-billets, perfume, and other Mazda-made objects.
The Hadhânaêpata branch is lifted up with sanctity and presented to Ahura Mazda and the good waters.
The good waters receive Zaothras, Haoma, milk, Hadhânaêpata, Haoma-water, the stone, and the iron mortar. They are described as having the Haoma with them and as beneficial.

l: Prayer for blessings, Yasna, Yasna XXIV.
s: The timely prayer for blessings approaches in the due course of the ritual and is presented as an offering. It is also described as the prayer of the holy lord of the ritual order.

l: recollection and practice of the good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna, Yasna XXIV.
s: The recollection and practice of the good Mazdayasnian Religion are presented together with the timely prayer, the heard recital of the Gâthas, and other ritual offerings.

l: Fire of Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XXIV.
s: The Fire of Ahura Mazda receives offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. Its perfume is presented as belonging to the Fire, and the Fire is called the lofty lord of entire holy creation.
Sraosha (Obedience), described as blessed and Righteous, receives the presented offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.

The Bountiful Immortals receive the presented offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. They are described as ruling and disposing all aright, ever-living, ever-helpful, and abiding with the Good Mind.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna XXIV.
s: The Fravashis of the saints receive offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. The presentation includes the Fravashis of saints who are dead and living.
The Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, identified as saint, receives offerings for sacrifice, propitiation, and praise.

l: people who love Righteousness, Yasna, Yasna XXIV.
s: The Fravashi of the people who love Righteousness receives offerings together with all the holy Fravashis of the saints.
The good Mazdayasnian Faith is associated with the recollection and practice that are presented as ritual offerings.
Righteousness is the seed possessed by the Mazda-made objects that are offered and presented. The people who love Righteousness are included among those whose Fravashi receives offerings.

The unit concerns worship offered to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Haoma, Fire, the good Mazdayasnian Religion, the good Mazdayasnian law, and the Mãthra Spenta. It describes ritual objects and substances, including Haoma, waters, mortars, Baresman, prayers, Gâthas, and perfumed wood-billets. It praises Mazda-made and holy knowledge, law, fire, winds, mountains, and Yazads. It also identifies the Mãthra Spenta with the law pronounced against the Daêvas, the Zarathustrian law, and Mazda-made understanding.
The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped as those who rule aright and dispose of all aright. They are also worshipped with Ahura Mazda.
Haoma is worshipped as flesh and branch, together with the Zaothras and beneficial waters. Haoma-water is worshipped for the beneficial waters.

l: good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna, Yasna XXV.
s: The good Mazdayasnian Religion is worshipped in connection with the remembrance and practice of the religion, and with the Mãthra. It is described as maintained in the understanding of the saint.
Fire is addressed as Ahura Mazda's son and the holy lord of the ritual order, and is worshipped. All the Fires are also worshipped, along with wood-billets bearing the Fire's perfume.
Ahura Mazda is worshipped as resplendent and glorious, together with the Bountiful Immortals. Fire is identified as Ahura Mazda's son.
The good Mazdayasnian law is worshipped as the most true religious Knowledge, Mazda-made and holy.

The Mãthra Spenta is worshipped as verily glorious and as the law pronounced against the Daêvas, the Zarathustrian law, and its long descent. It is also identified with the heart-devoted and bounteous Mãthra, the science that is Mãthra Spenta, and Mazda-made innate and derived understanding.

The unit praises, invokes, and worships the good, heroic, and bountiful Fravashis of the saints and related holy beings. It specifically honors the Fravashi of Ahura Mazda, the Fravashis of named holy figures, and the Fravashis, souls, and other faculties of holy men and women, including the dead, living, unborn, teachers, disciples, and children. It worships the Fravashis of the saints from Gaya Maretan to Saoshyant, the victorious.

l: Fravashis of the saints (ancient lore), Yasna, Yasna XXVI.
s: The Fravashis are praised, invoked, and worshipped as good, heroic, and bountiful. The unit honors the Fravashis of Ahura Mazda, the saints, holy teachers and disciples, holy children, and all holy men and women from Gaya Maretan to Saoshyant.
Ahura Mazda's Fravashi is worshipped as the greatest, best, most beautiful, firmest, wisest, and best in form. It attains its ends most because of Righteousness.

The saints are honored through worship of their Fravashis, souls, spirits, consciences, intelligences, and lives. The unit includes dead, living, and unborn saints, as well as holy men, women, teachers, disciples, and children.
